data_fields.name: market_cost
data_fields.donor_constant: Hochelaga 160 (150+10), Stadacona 140 (125+15), New York 105 (80+25), paid before the sale

data_fields.name: price_band
data_fields.donor_constant: per good, dollars per pelt, lo + k*rnd: Hochelaga beaver .75 to .95; Stadacona mink .85 to 1.15; New York mink 1.05 to 1.20, fox 1.10 to 1.35

data_fields.name: route_roll_faces
data_fields.donor_constant: d10 (1 to 10), Stadacona 1-2 lose beaver, 3-6 safe, 7-8 lose all, 9-10 lose fox; New York 1-2 dead, 3-6 safe, 7-8 lose all, 9-10 halve mink and beaver

data_fields.name: halve_factor
data_fields.donor_constant: 0.5 on the price of the named goods after a route event

data_fields.name: inventory_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: 190 pelts across four kinds, over-cap restarts the run

data_fields.name: start_savings
data_fields.donor_constant: 600 savings at the start of a run

best_idea: A market is data on the zone (cost, one price band per good, one d10 route table), and one trip function pays the cost first, rolls each price on arrival, rolls the route once, and settles the sale as exact count times price.
decision_why: The market-as-data shape (per-zone price bands, cost paid up front, one route roll with a table) fits zones as data; the year cycle, the BASIC rounding idiom and the Java fall-through and missing savings check must not be copied.
acceptance: A server test: a merchant zone with a band of 85-115 cents for a unit rolls one price on arrival in that band; selling 20 units pays exactly 20 times that price; a route roll of 1-2 takes the stock named in the zone data; a trip whose cost exceeds savings is refused and changes nothing.
